keyFindings.description: cmd/dispatch now compiles internal/roles, internal/store, internal/session and internal/kvwatch (go list -deps ./cmd/dispatch), and cmd/listener compiles internal/roles; the dispatch_server and listener_command path filters name none of them, so a later change to internal/roles skips dispatch_multiprocess, dispatch_memory and envoy_infra_go. The workflow comment at :167-180 asks the PR that adds the import to add the package.

The listener's role forward (RequestCoreTo) now sets Nats-Msg-Id for every envelope, without the DedupeKeyNamesTheUpstreamEvent guard the window uses (async.go:189); two distinct role messages that share a caller-chosen dedupe key get their second stored copy dropped by the stream, a lost delivery once INFRA-594 delivers serving-port holders from the stream. Not in the plan or the CHANGELOG.

0136 starts with alter table events add column and ends with two drop index, each ACCESS EXCLUSIVE held until the migration's transaction commits, so reads of events wait through all three index builds too; the migration comment, cmd/dispatch/README.md:954-955 and CHANGELOG.md:928 say only writes are held.

No Contract change census: Dispatch's role-routed events stop being published on notifications.role.<id> (a process boundary), the listener's forward gains a Nats-Msg-Id header, bus.Sender and outbox.Publisher gain methods (package boundary), and two indexes are dropped / one column added under a rollout with the old build.

The grace timer returns natsLost without reading Connected() again; ConnectionChanged is closed from nats.go's serialized callback goroutine, and onReconnect runs restoreSubscriptions and rewatch synchronously (recovery.go:20-82), so a reconnect callback queued behind a slow earlier one releases the hold of a connected holder; ensureConnWithContext (nats.go:779-800) likewise waits on that channel alone where it polled every 10 ms.
Nothing waits for outbox Run before shutdown closes the pool (shutdown.go:108-110), so the documented graceful record and Release can fail and the standby waits for the lapse.
A holdLost that came from the record's hold check (publisher.go:286-290) neither releases nor stops the hold, so its renewal goroutine can keep running beside the next TryHold's.
The deadline is checked before window.pin, which can wait up to 5 s for a connection (async.go:159-170) and then write after the deadline.
A skipped role route (no claim, holder gone, echo) is recorded as a reached send (batch.go:361-363) and counts the event as sent in the 'sent batch' log line and its span.

Docs that do not match the code: a stopping holder sends nothing more and releases what is in flight (not 'finishes the one in flight', also lease.go:127); a batch past its deadline is left unrecorded, not released (:67, publisher.go:356); a gone holder's claim is resolved once more, two reads in all (:56, role.go:113); AGENTS.md:2208 names migration 0130 for duty.Hold (it is 0135); running-dispatch.md:293-295's ten seconds does not hold for an idle holder behind a silent cut.
